Hi everyone,

I asked few days aog about a model that I am trying to fit see the link (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/lavaan/YSmKV-FcW1Y)

Thanks to the great help of Jeremy Miles I got an identified model and everything went well.

However, when I got the results for my latent variables (2 formative exogenous variables, and 1 reflective endogenous variable) I tried to rescale the results to 0-100 scale and plot the results using ggtern plot to see the behavior of the endogenous variable given the two formative latent variable as follows:

#LV1 formative variable
#LV2 formative variable
#LV3 reflective variable

pred <- as.data.frame(lavPredict(dataset))

scores <- lavScores(dataset, scaling = FALSE, ignore.constraints = FALSE,
                    remove.duplicated = TRUE, remove.empty.cases = TRUE)

library(scales)
library(ggtern)

SLV1 <- rescale(pred$LV1, to = c(0,100), from =c(-0.2111946, -0.1960924)) #rescaled LV1
SLV2 <- rescale(pred$LV2, to = c(0,100), from = c(0.4722854, 2.767426)) #rescaled LV2
SLV3 <- rescale(pred$LV3, to = c(0,100), from = c(-1.878566266, 4.322315)) #rescaled LV3

ggtern(data=pred, aes(x=SLV1, y=SLV2, z=LV3)) + geom_point()

I got results basically identical for each variable. As an example:

ٍSLV1 values: 0, 2, 4, 5. 7, 9, ..., 100
SLV2 values: 0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, ..., 100
SLV3 values: 0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, ..., 100

Why there is no variability, why there is no scattering for the data according to the change in SLV1 and SLV2

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Model results are giving same range of values
parts:
Osama,
  It is harder to spot what exactly went wrong without a reproducible example.  However, I noticed that you told the ggtern() function to use pred as the data for the graph, but you never added the rescaled variables to that data frame.  I believe that your aes() function is just relabeling the old variables as the new variables (in two cases).  Could that be the problem?  What happens if you make a scatterplot matrix of the six variables (original scale and rescaled)?

Keith
